name: Sargon
title: Conquering King of Assyria
summary: Sargon II was king of Assyria and founder of the Sargonid dynasty. He is known in the Bible for completing the conquest of Samaria and the deportation of the Northern Kingdom of Israel in 722 BC. He is the only Assyrian king with this name mentioned directly in the Bible, in Isaiah 20:1.

keyEvents.title: The Conquest of Samaria
keyEvents.description: Sargon II completed the siege of Samaria that his predecessor Shalmaneser V had begun, and deported the people of Israel to Assyria. This marked the end of the Northern Kingdom of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Deportation and Resettlement of Peoples
keyEvents.description: Sargon deported the Israelites and settled foreign peoples in Samaria, leading to the emergence of the Samaritans as a mixed people with a syncretistic religion.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Isaiah's Prophecy
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah mentions Sargon directly by name in connection with a campaign against the Philistine city of Ashdod, where Isaiah was asked to go as a prophetic sign.

keyEvents.title: Assyria's Expansion and God's Judgment
keyEvents.description: Sargon was an instrument of God's judgment on Israel because of their sin and idolatry. The prophets interpreted the Assyrian invasion as God's punishment upon a disobedient people.

keyEvents.title: Assyrian Threat to Judah
keyEvents.description: During Sargon's reign, Assyria continued to threaten the kingdom of Judah, and his military campaigns in the region created fear and unrest among Judah's inhabitants and their neighboring peoples.
